subject: Force observer to run, or input to invalidate?

messages.author: 2c21699eecac9408
messages.subject: Force observer to run, or input to invalidate?
parts:
Hey guys. I've been using Shiny for a very long time now, but I can't figure out a clean way to do this.

I have two selectizeInput elements. The choices in the second are computed based on the selection in the first. Think Role, Colleague - you select "Programmer", second input shows you a list of names, you select "Michael", I print you his salary.

Now here's the annoying part. The choices in the second input frequently overlap. So after you select Michael the Programmer, you decide to look up Michael from PR. PR is a one-man department, so when you select PR in the first input, the second input triggers updateSelectInput(session, "name", choices = c("Michael"))..the input is again "Michael", and an observer that is only watching the second field will not invalidate!

The way I deal with this currently is by checking if the current choice is the same as the one I'm updating to, and adding whitespace to the new value to differentiate it if so. I've tried several more beautiful hacks in an attempt to invalidate the input when updating to it, but this is the simplest one that still worked. Can we just do observer::flush or something?

messages.author: 2c21699eecac9408
messages.subject: Re: Force observer to run, or input to invalidate?
parts: Well, this is embarassing. I managed to solve the problem by using a named list so that labels that are the same share different values. I'm still curious if there's a way to force an invalidation, but I no longer have a particular need for it.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Force observer to run, or input to invalidate?
parts:
Two thoughts:

1) When you call updateSelectInput, it seems like you should also be passing value="" to clear out the current selection.
2) It doesn't seem right to me that "Michael" should be interpreted the same in both departments. Do you know that selectInput options can have values that are distinct from labels? If the "choices" argument is a named list, the names are used as the display labels and the elements are what actually get passed back to server.R. So you could have employee IDs as the values and the employee names as the names.
